items.heading: Search "Science Careers That Involve
items.text: Search "science careers that involve travel" and you will find lists that treat it as one glamorous destination job. It is not. It is a real, useful filter you can apply to several already-established science fields, geology, environmental science, marine biology, wildlife biology, and science journalism, each of which already has its own degree path, employer base, and honest pay ceiling on this site.

items.heading: Before Comparing Tracks, Set Expectations
items.text: Before comparing tracks, set expectations correctly. In almost every one of these six fields, "travel" means one of a few concrete things, not a rotating global itinerary.

columns: What the travel actually looks like
rows: Field seasons at remote sites, drilling camps, or offshore rigs, a few weeks to months a year, mostly domestic
B.Sc/M.Sc Geology or Applied Geology, step for ONGC/PSU entry, or a state/GSI recruitment exam
Repeated short site visits for baseline sampling, project-by-project, almost entirely domestic
M.Sc Environmental Science, covered in depth in our environmental science careers guide
Coastal fieldwork most of the year, occasional research-vessel cruises of a few weeks
M.Sc Marine Biology/Oceanography plus CSIR-UGC NET or a DBT/ICMR-JRF entrance route
Extended stretches living inside or near forests, reserves, and field stations
B.Sc/M.Sc Wildlife Science or Zoology, often with a WII or NGO fellowship as the real entry door

items.heading: A Field Season
items.text: A field season of a few weeks to a few months at a remote site, camp, or field station, mostly within India.

items.heading: Repeated Short Trips
items.text: Repeated short trips to a project site for sampling, surveying, or assessment, then weeks back at a desk.

items.heading: An Occasional Research Cruise, Expedition,
items.text: An occasional research cruise, expedition, or assignment, genuinely exciting, but infrequent, not year-round.
